description: Replace all of a site's user redirect rules in one call, all or nothing: pass either `rules` or `text` in the `_redirects` format, one `from to [status]` per line. Use this, or `edit_redirects`, for bulk work, such as moving a list of redirects from another host, rather than many `add_redirect` calls. Rules are checked in the order given, before the live deploy's file rules, and the status defaults to 301. A rule sent with the `id` of an existing rule keeps it. Pass the `version` from `list_redirects` to refuse the change if the rules changed since: the error is `StaleVersion`, with the latest version, so read the rules again and reapply the change. One invalid rule refuses the call with `InvalidRules`, listing each error by the rule's `index` or the text's `line`. The file rules don't change. Redirects apply only on the organization's own custom domains (`CustomDomainRequired` otherwise). Visitors get the change within about 5 minutes. Rules left out are deleted, and an empty list deletes them all: confirm with the user before dropping rules.

partition.description: Data partition the site lives in. Omit to use the user's home partition.

rules.description: The new list, in the order rules are checked. Pass this or `text`.

from.description: Source path: exact (`/old-page`), with `:name` placeholders (`/blog/:year/:slug`), or ending in `/*` (`/docs/*`). No query string.

id.description: An existing rule's id, to keep it.

status.description: 301, 302, 303, 307 or 308. Defaults to 301, a permanent move. Use 302 or 307 for a temporary one.

to.description: Destination: a path starting with `/`, or an http(s) URL. `:splat` fills in what `*` matched, and `:name` a placeholder's value. The request's query string is carried over.

text.description: The new list in the `_redirects` format, one `from to [status]` per line, such as `/old /new 301`. Pass this or `rules`.

version.description: The `version` the rules were read at, from `list_redirects`. Omit to replace whatever the latest list is.

name: set_redirects
